content:
Alex Chen: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'fastpath' onboarding flow that gives a quick pass/fail for new model uploads. goal: 30s feedback for devs. full bench (the deep perf suite) still required before admit, but fastpath catches glaring compatibility and obvious perf regressions. thoughts?

Priya Patel: +1 on fast feedback. what exactly are we running in the 30s window?

Alex Chen: idea: three lightweight checks — 1) metadata/manifest sanity (shapes, dtype, entrypoint), 2) tokenizer roundtrip & sample inference (5 short prompts), 3) microbench warmup (small batch, short seqlen) to detect immediate OOMs/slow kernels. no long tail evals.

Jon B.: include KV cache layout check. we've had models that look fine but blow up when kv cache is requested. small kv synthetic replay would be quick.

Marta G: worry: false positives will annoy teams and cause gating friction. if fastpath fails we should clearly mark "fastpath-fail" vs "requires-fullbench" and make it easy to request re-run. also consider making fastpath advisory for community uploads, mandatory for internal CI.

Sam R: ops note — metrics we should emit from fastpath: latency_p50/p95, small-sample mem-peak, tokenization-incorrect-count, kv-shape-mismatch boolean. tag with model_sha and runner-profile. rollout plan: start advisory for 2 weeks, then opt-in block for newly onboarded models, then mandatory for all uploads after we iterate.

onboard-bot: Automated run started for model "mosaic-guest-v4" (sha: 8a7f). fastpath-run-id: fp-20240601-42.

Priya Patel: what about versioned compat signatures? if we compute a small compatibility signature (kv-dim, vocab-hash, dtype, layer-count) and store it in registry, we can detect obvious mismatches across runners.

Alex Chen: yes — propose adding artifact field compat_signature_v1 and store as part of model metadata. that becomes a cheap filter in the intake gateway. compatibility signature should be deterministic and small.

Jon B.: for the microbench, prefer measuring warmup kernel selection time rather than full throughput. many regressions are kernel selection or memcpy surprises. a 10-step warmup with telemetry hooks should catch ~80% of regressions.

Marta G: interface boundary question — who owns the fastpath check code? eng-ml or eng-runtime? we need to avoid duplicate test implementations. my vote: shared small library in /libs/onboard-smoke used by both the console (for local checks) and the runtime for server-side checks. keep it language-agnostic via a tiny CLI shim.

Alex Chen: agreed. sketch CLI: 
```
redwood-onboard --model ./pkg.tar.gz \
  --fastpath \
  --checks meta,tokenize,kv,microbench \
  --timeout 30s \
  --out /tmp/fp-result.json
```
Result includes fields: status: PASS|FAIL|WARN, failing_checks: [], metrics: {latency_p50,mem_peak}, compat_signature.

Sam R: ops integration — ensure results emit to metrics backend and to model registry as "last_fastpath_status". also capture minimal artifacts (tiny logs + sample tokens) for debugging. retention: 30d for artifacts, metrics indefinitely.

Priya Patel: detection thresholds: let's avoid black/white for some checks. tokenization_sample_mismatch > 0 => WARN, but kv_shape_mismatch => FAIL. microbench latency > baseline*3 => WARN (but if mem_peak > node_memory => FAIL). we can iterate on thresholds.

Jon B.: to reduce false negatives, add a randomized small input set (5 seeds) to the tokenizer and microbench step. keeps runtime small but increases coverage.

Marta G: ops risk — this will add noise to our intake pipeline. suggest a 3-stage rollout: advisory (no gating), soft-block (gateway warns and needs manual override), hard-block (reject until fixed). document clear escape hatches for support.

Alex Chen: wrap-up / action items:
- Priya: draft compat_signature_v1 schema (fields + deterministic hash) — due EOW.
- Jon: prototype kv cache synthetic check + 10-step warmup runner — PoC by Tue.
- Marta: write short roll-out playbook and developer UX (how to re-run & appeal) — due next Fri.
- Sam: metrics/registry integration plan + retention policy — sync Wed.

Alex Chen: tag @onboard-bot at end of rollout to start advisory runs automatically. thanks all :thumbsup:

onboard-bot: ack — scheduled advisory runs begin 2024-06-05 for new uploads.
